Hi! 

First off, thanks for coming to our wedding! This is an app called __WIGI__, short for _"Wherever I'm going, I'm happy you're coming"_. It's a line from our first dance song, _Pretty Boy_ by The Neighbourhood. This is a list of locations Alyssa and I have been throughout our time together. Not exhaustive, but I did my best to include everywhere we took pictures. This is the first card of 80-or-so locations. You can swipe through the cards horizontally (swipe left!), and you can swipe through the pictures on each individual card. Each card has a short blurb about the location, and below that is an interactive Google Maps pin of the location itself. Scroll through the cards and travel with us!

For the programmers here -- the source code can be found on [GitHub](https://github.com/ajsampang67/wigi). It's a pretty simple widget-based app written in Dart with Flutter. Very similar to Javascript with React Native. Highly recommend! The app took me about a month to create, from knowing nothing about Dart/Flutter to what you're looking at now. It's deployed on an EC2 instance using docker-compose, served via nginx webserver alongside my personal website.

This first pin below is Jade Mountain, our honeymoon destination!

Welcome to our wedding venue, The BRIX on the Fox! This building is originally a condensed milk factory, built in 1880. In 2018, Rob and Tone Gorman renovated the space into a one-stop wedding venue overlooking the Fox River.

In May of 2022, Alyssa and I were in the middle of our venue tours. The BRIX was the third spot we'd visit, but the last one we'd need. Alyssa and I got in the car and discussed how this was the first venue we could picture getting married. On the trip from The BRIX to the next venue, _Pretty Boy_ by The Neighbourhood came on, and we immediately knew it would be our first dance song.

The Brix is a pretty cool venue. Rob and Tone were purposeful in their renovation of The Brix. The acoustics of the Two-Sixty are targeted such that the dance floor will BOOM without flooding too much noise into the seating area. The ceilings are set up with infrastructure for separating the room into areas for the ceremony, and then shortly after for cocktail hour and reception. Rob and Tone showed their drive to make a beautiful wedding space, and in turn, made the decision easy to make our love official in this space.

Alyssa and I met at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign. Here we took a GenEd, Latin American Studies together. We met when our mutual friends sat together, where I took the empty seat next to Alyssa. We chatted through the class and parted ways. A few days later, I go over to my friend's apartment to grab some of my beers from their fridge and lo-and-behold! Alyssa was there! She was friends with my neighboring apartment as they were both in UIUC's nursing program.

From there, we were lucky enough to hang out more and get to know one another. We went on lunch dates and study dates. We spent time at the Underground Library enjoying Bad and Boujee and Pillow Talk music videos on repeat. We spent hours watching the Jimmy Neutron Movie while writing an essay about Latin American coups. We enjoyed our midnight cheese snacks and insomnia cookies. We studied hard, made memories, and somehow came out with our degrees!

The UI Ice Arena was a pretty regular place for the two of us. We were at UIUC right at the tail end of the Blackhawks' run, resulting in myself having some interest in learning how to skate in hockey skates. Alyssa, more of a natural, had 14 years of figure skating experience already under her belt! The pictures you see above are July of 2016 from our first ice skating date, and again in December of 2017 for a special holiday-themed skate

Chicago is where Alyssa and I had our first _real real_ date. Ally had told me that despite her living in Chicago, she never went to any of the tourist spots. She'd never been to The Bean, gone to the top of the Sears Tower, or ridden the Ferris wheel at Navy Pier! I grabbed us some disposable cameras and took her on a tourist date around the city. The first few photos you see are just that; they're a bit vintage looking from the cheap film of the disposable. 

Other than that, it's only natural we'd visit the city fairly often. We liked to go in the winter to visit the Christkindlmarket, do some Macy's window shopping, and take some pictures with the big tree.

Curtis is a nice farm out in Champaign. Alyssa is a real Autumn Ally and makes sure we visit a pumpkin patch every year. They've got a big chair, petting zoo, and delicious hot apple cider! 

_"I like it! We go there a lot when we were young spring chickens, and I like it. What are you saying about it Alf? That you like it?"_ - Alyssa Nicole
December of 2016 was the first holiday season we spent together. Enjoy a quick couple of pictures of Alyssa spending time with the Sampang's on Christmas!

Just after the New Year of 2017, Alyssa got us some Blackhawks tickets for our first NHL game together! This is the day we first consider ourselves "official", January 5th of 2016. Since then we celebrate every 5th of the month as "Buns Day" (like pork bun, because Ally is cute like a pork bun). We make sure to have a nice dinner date, or watch a movie, or at very least fit in an extra face kiss!

On this day I actually accidentally threw out our Hawks tickets before the game! This was back when they __only__ accepted paper tickets. The hotel had already taken away our trash, and I begged the front desk to dig through the trash and retrieve it for us. Lucky for us, they called back half an hour later, and found it! Alyssa and I attended the game and had a fantastic time. Patrick Kane scored the GWG in OT on a breakaway as Alyssa took a bathroom break.

Beckwith is a residential community at UIUC dedicated to students with severe physical disabilities, in which Beckwith assists these residents in the transition to independent living. Alyssa worked as a CNA assisting students with some of their daily tasks, such as getting ready for bed or preparing meals for the day. 

The photos in this slide are from the yearly Beckwith semi-formal 2018 and 2019! We got to dress up with a theme and have dinner with everyone. The people Alyssa got to work with were always so sweet, Lauren was a huge Panic! at the Disco fan like myself, and our good friend Danny who always made us laugh went on to become a successful lawyer after school!

I hate rollercoasters, but Alyssa loves them! Somehow she got me to go along with her in May of 2017 and I went on _almost_ every ride with her. I will never go on giant drops, and I hate wooden roller coasters. Alyssa had a great time though.

_"Aj hated every second of it"_ - Alyssa Nicole

In the summer of 2017 I got my first "real job" in the form of an internship at Nutanix, a cloud computing company providing servers and software for cloud computing. Alyssa was sweet enough to take the time to come out east and visit me! Here we went to the Sarah P. Duke Gardens, a restaurant hosting a wall-art coloring book event, and a benefit dinner for Durham's _Families Moving Forward_ organization.

Everyone knows the Christkindlmarket in Chicago! Alyssa and I try to go every year. The pictures you see here are from 2017, 2019, and 2021. So we really have a 50% success rate. We tried to go this past year, 2022, but the line was far too long! We opted instead to take a walk through the Millennium Park and grab some sushi at a restaurant nearby. The pictures from that date can be found on the Chicago slide.

Sakanaya is one of the nicer sushi places out in Champaign. We didn't come here often, just to celebrate bigger events. This last picture was probably the last time we went, Alyssa's birthday in 2018! On my sushi rankings list, this falls in the "B Tier" (which, I still like a lot!). 

---
**S Tier** - Sushi Dokku (West Loop) (Same as booze box), 🍣Ohshima (Los Angeles, CA)

**A Tier** - Kura (Schaumburg), Sushi-san, Sushi Taku (Wicker Park), Maple and ash (Gold Coast)

**B Tier** - Kizuna sushi bistro (Glenn Elynn), Sushi Ukai (La Grange), Wild Tuna (Naperville), Sushi Time (Elmhurst), **Sakanaya (Champaign)**, Kamehachi (Gold Coast)

**C Tier** - Umami sushi (O’Hare), Sushi + (Lakeview), Shakou (Park Ridge), Mizu Sushi House (Orland Park)

**F** - Wu’s House (Orland Park x 2) (BAD, DO NOT COME BACK)

---

Riu Santa Fe was actually mine and Alyssa's very first all-inclusive vacation and it was AWESOME! Big thank you to our friend Lea who not only accompanied us on this trip, but really spearheaded the idea. We had a great time with our friends, we got some delicious drinks and laid out on the beach. Alyssa and I decided to go out on an excursion to swim with some whale sharks near La Paz, check it out next!

La Paz was a really cool visit for us! The main event of the trip was swimming with some whale sharks. We threw on fins and wetsuits and got diving! This small charter boat drove us to an area near whale sharks, and we just dove in and swam alongside them. It was horrifying and fascinating all at once. 
Before some hard swimming against the currents, we went to the city of La Paz! Here we did some shopping and got lunch. It was a nice catered lunch the whale-shark-diving group had organized for us. This was the first of many south-of-the-US excursions to come!

Back in the US and still in our summer after graduating from UIUC, we wanted to continue on our little adventures. We were craving a spot to hike, and Ally had the great idea of hiking Starved Rock! I had only been there as a kid to go fishing, so although I've been here tens of times, it was really cool to get a completely new look at the place. Alyssa took us to some familiar trails she had gone through before, and we got some nice pictures out of it.
Brookfield Zoo is solid, but admittedly Alyssa and I have a bad habit of going a bit too late when all the animals are asleep! But enjoy some pictures of us with the free-roaming peacocks!

In June of 2018, Ally and I went up to Ann Arbor, Michigan so I could show her around the city and visit my sister. We had a great time kayaking and checking out the local museum. The campus had a festival at the time as well, so we got to hangout on the quad with some drinks and live music!

column4:
As Ally and I finished up school and moved back home, we were no longer near our regular Curtis pumpkin patch and had to find a new one! Luckily enough, Bengston's was nearby and became our norm. Here we have pictures from Octobers of 2018 and 2019. Look how much we grew in one year!!! wild

_"I love the highland cows. the highland cows are my favorite."_ - Alyssa Nicole

In October of 2018 we decided to visit Mickey's Halloween Party at Disneyland! Despite hating rollercoasters, I actually do love Space Mountain. One of my all-time favorite pics of the two of us is on the third slide here -- wild excitement coming down from Ghost Galaxy! We got our matching shirts and visited Mickey's House. Alyssa played the piano for Mr. Mouse. A very successful visit!

Alyssa and I were actually in California primarily due to my own work -- Liferay had flown all the employees down for a conference. Talking with all the employees, obviously someone had to know the best sushi spot in town! One of the highest references was Ohshima sushi, which we landed on as it was so close to Disneyland Park. This was our first real Omakase experience, and it SLAPPED. This sushi restaurant topped our rankings list until just recently -- when Chicago's BoozeBox dethroned them. Still, Ohshima is no joke, and we'll definitely be back in the future!

**B Tier** - Maple and ash (Gold Coast), Sushi Ukai (La Grange), Wild Tuna (Naperville), Sushi Time (Elmhurst), Sakanaya (Champaign), Kamehachi (Gold Coast)

Good ol' Oak Forest, my hometown! This is really just a hodgepodge of pictures from around the area. This very first picture is from Halloween of 2018, when our friend (and my groomsman!) Anthony put together a Halloween party for all of us. It was a BLAST, everyone's costumes were great and we were JAMMIN'!

The next set of photos is Alyssa and I with our Build-a-Bear, Bearald. We sleep with him every night! If one of us is missing from the bed, he's our backup cuddler.

Third set is Alyssa and I in Allie's garage. She was always a great host, so this was a commonplace for us to be found while we were all still in Oak Forest.

Following that is a quick Christmas, actually this past Christmas, at Auntic Dic's! They always have such sparkling decorations, it's hard to pass up the photo op.

Second to last we see a paint-n-sip night we had at Sam and Seans, where I painted a canvas for our lil' animals, PB n' Jams

And last but not least, The Shulls' bridal shower in Midlo! A really sweet yellow-flowery themed bridal shower thrown by a beautiful couple, whose wedding we would attend just a few months later.

This sushi boat was solid but we would later come back here and find old, slimy sushi and steamed rice that clearly was not prepared with rice vinegar. -10/10, would not recommend

In December of 2018, Alyssa and I were pretty close and I wanted to get her a really special gift. Over our time together I found she had a particular interest in wolves... so I got her one! Kind of. Out near Indianapolis there is a wolf sanctuary, "Wolf Park". Here we sponsored a wolf, Timber. I took Alyssa on a trip to Indianapolis which would end with a surprise visit to her birthday gift, a full meet-and-greet with Timber (and fellow wolves at the park).
That weekend we went to the Indianapolis Museum of Art at Newfields, which had a stunning geometric wall we took photos with! Following that we had dinner and a show; we went to see A Christmas Carol at Indianapolis' Civic Theatre. We'd go on to visit Timber a couple more times as the sponsorship lasted a year.

Laugh Factory was a last-second date Alyssa and I put together. We hadn't gone to a stand-up show together before, so we found these tickets on Groupon on a whim. Turned out we'd end up having near-front-row seats next to this nice couple. We chatted with them throughout the show, and then stayed a bit after the show to hangout with them and the comedian, Akeem Woods! He was really friendly and absolutely hilarious.

Lake Geneva is easily one of mine and Alyssa's favorite vacation spots! Unfortunately we only have a picture here from 2019, but out first-ever trip to Lake Geneva was back in 2017, when I was still 20 and therefore not old enough to drink! Ally and I stayed at The Lodge, a spa hotel. Ally got a drink at dinner, while I snuck some sips when the waitress wasn't looking! In hindsight, they probably didn't care, and it was just a silly experience. Since then, we've come back to Lake Geneva to visit The Abbey Resort for another spa vacation, and I'd really highly recommend that place! Alongside your massage, you get a few hours in a relaxing pool area where you can just sit, read, and unwind. We love our spa vacations! We've come here for wine tastings as well -- my favorite "gift wine" was one we found at a small winery, "Sexual Chocolate". It's actually a widely available red wine. If you see a red wine with a bunch of handwritten-looking writing as the label, grab it! it's a delicious red wine to pair with chocolate, and is Advanced Sommelier approved (Thanks Igor!).
Anyways, the pictures you see here are from 2019 at the Ice Castles! Out in Lake Geneva they create a giant castle out of ice, filled with slides and mazes, as well as some drinks and snacks.

Just a quick one here, Mizu Sushi house! We love our sushi boats! This place was really solid, it's in my "C-Tier" which sounds low, but it's definitely a place I'd gladly go back! This tends to be the "All you can eat" category for me, so although the quality isn't S-A-or-B tier, its' still plenty good to eat, and will always satisfy that sushi craving

---

**C Tier** - Umami sushi (O’Hare), Sushi + (Lakeview), Shakou (Park Ridge), **Mizu Sushi House (Orland Park)**

**F** - Wu’s House (Orland Park x 2) (BAD, DO NOT COME BACK)

---

Out in May of 2019, Ally and I decided to visit Colorado! We chose to check out Colorado Springs, and one of the big attractions out that way is the Royal Gorge Bridge & Park. Royal Gorge is a 1250ft deep canyon just outside of Cañon City. We came here off a suggestion from our friend Pooja who had just gone earlier in the year! The canyon was beautiful and honestly pretty nerve-wracking! The bridge is lined with the flags of all 50 states. Going across the bridge had us holding pretty tight to the railings and nervously looking down. We went on a zipline that went across the gorge, and it was exhilarating! There is also a gondola that goes across the canyon, which you can see us taking pictures in. Lastly, on a lower point of the canyon, is a cave system! We went spelunking and got to see some stalagmites and stalactites. At one point of the tour, they turn off all the lights, and you can't even see your hand in front of your face. Our final stop on our way back to Colorado Springs was an old prison museum, in which they had an old retired gas chamber. Spooky stuff! Right up Ally's alley.

Having flown in-and-out of Denver, we had to hit up the Blue Moon Brewing Company! Blue Moon is my go-to beer, so this was a really cool experience for us. We got to do flights of their experimental beers at the time, and they actually hold a leaderboard of the top-requested beers! I remember here they had been trialing their "Iced Coffee Blonde", which I was excited to see in stores just a few months later for the winter seasonal beers.

The Denver Botanic Gardens was beautiful! We were on our way to the airport when we found we had a few extra hours, so we decided to stop by, and what a great decision that was! We like to visit the botanic gardens of the cities we visit, and this one was my second favorite after Chicago's. They have this large honeycomb-themed pyramid near the center of the garden which is used for research and BEES! We got to see a lot of pretty tulips as they were in-season, and some really wild trees and plants. Denver's Botanic Garden is a great example of placing greenery in a busy city, and always worth the stop.

Our most-anticipated part of this trip, Garden of the Gods! Garden of the Gods is a registered National Natural Landmark with giant spikes of red rock shooting out of the ground. We started off our visit with a Wolf Walk -- again we found an organization which rescued wolves, and this one actually let us walk them! The photos you see are with Colorado Wolf Adventures. These guys were HUGE! Their paws were the size of my face. Still, they acted very similarly to dogs and even let us rub their bellies. After our walk, we went off into the park and got to take some pictures on a light hike through the "garden".

Alyssa and I drove down with the whole Sampang family to St. Louis for the wonderful Shredl wedding! The city of St. Louis was really pretty, the arch was even larger than I imagined and the view from up there was incredible. Having a beautiful event to dress up for doesn't hurt either, Alyssa and I were really happy with how well my tie matched her dress! Hoping we get some opportunities to get back to St. Louis in the future.

Chicago Botanic Garden is almost a yearly visit for us! We love going on walks, and one of the best places to do that is out at the Chicago Botanic Garden. Our first date at this location was in September of 2019, where Ally learned about my love of Bees & Bonsais. We've been back a few times since then, once for the Night of 1,000 Jack-o-Lanterns and again for the Lightscape during Winter. Our most recent visit was in May of this year just a relaxing date out. As members of the Chicago Botanic Garden, we'll be back several times next year!

_"ummm my favorite part is the um bonsais"_ - Alyssa Nicole

Alyssa finished her nursing degree out at Loyola in December of 2019. It was a grind as she studied hard every week and took her long commutes out to rotational assignments, she toughed through it and got it done! The photos here are at her graduation ceremony. Look at all those flowers!!

As a graduation gift to Alyssa, we went off to The Haven in Cancun for another all-inclusive vacation! Her RN-BSN was a TON of work and deserved a good relaxing time off. The Haven is our current all-time favorite all-inclusive. The food, events, rooms, staff, are all the best we've had in all the places we've gone! The restaurants were some of the best. Most all-inclusive restaurants __look__ five-star, but these __tasted__ five-star too! Ally and I had steaks, seafood, mexican food, you name it. The shows were really great too. all-inclusive shows can be nice, but the production value of these shows blew us out of the water. Early in the trip we had gone to a drinks-and-bingo event in which I had a missed bingo, the staff was apologetic but it was no big deal. We missed out on a free private dinner on the beach, but there was plenty to do around so we didn't mind. We go off to our regular dinner followed by the late-night show, and to our surprise the same staff who organized the bingo is organizing the performance. He recognized us from earlier, and decided to give us VIP upper-deck private table seats! It was a nice unexpected bonus and made the trip all that much nicer. I can't say enough good things about this hotel. If you're looking for an all-inclusive, this is the one you need to go to!

_"My favorite all-inclusive we've gone to!"_ - Alyssa Nicole

In January of 2020, we took a vacation to Universal Studios. I hadn't been back since I was a kid, and as I was in town for work anyways, it seemed like the perfect combo to get Ally out here too so we could do some vacationing! Universal was awesome, did the standard items of taking a picture at the globe and going on the Studio tour! The "plane crash" wreck was really cool to see, and following that we got to see the froyo place from The Good Place! That was a huge bonus for us; we had been in the middle of watching ther series at the time, and didn't realize we'd be seeing the set that day. Alyssa got to get some butter beer and take a pic with Sirius Black, afterwards we got some donuts and got on our way!

The Hollywood Wax Museum was really cool! Admittedly Hollywood itself was a pretty painful tourist trap, but this museum I was happy to be as tourist as it gets. It was a little creepy, but you get over that feeling fast when you get to take pics with your favorite celebrities! Hilariously realistic, Ally got to take a pic with her favorite 22 Jump Street star Channing Tatum, and I got to spit bars with The Real Slim Shady.

_"Channing Tatum was really tall"_ - Alyssa Nicole

Much like the Chicago Botanic Gardens, the Shedd Aquarium is a regular date spot for us as well! Not many pictures over the years, but we tend to go here about once a year. We try to catch special events; this first set of pictures you see is from January 2020. For my Christmas gift, Alyssa took me to a meet-and-greet sea otters event! We got to touch their cute little tiny paws, feed them some sushi, and practice some training with them! Sea otters are my favorite animal, so Ally really hit the nail on the head with this one. Since then, we've gone on regular visits just to see some seahorses and belugas. Our most recent visit, the last two pictures, is from Jazzin' at the Shedd! An after-hours event where they serve drinks and play live jazz music in the lobby of the Shedd.

Safari Lake Geneva, in hindsight, was a really wild ride. We visited here in July of 2020, it's a safari where you just drive through the park in your own car! You can get buckets of feed to feed the animals, and let me tell you they are FEASTIN' in there. They have absolutely no fear, and as soon as you pull up, their heads are in the car! I wouldn't take anything more than a beater through this safari, as the animals are there for food and they're coming in hard to get it. Most of the animals were really cute and sweet, politely requested access in the window and then shoved their heads in our food bucket for a mouthful. One thing we learned though, is ostritches are RUDE. Straight up tries to take the whole bucket. Save some for your friends fatty. No wonder you can't fly. not even a real bird. figure it out

Off to our yearly orchard visit! In September of 2020 we went to All Seasons Orchard with some friends of ours from Ally's nursing school. The orchard was really nice, rows and rows of trees with different varieties to choose from. We also got a cool apple-picking bucket-on-a-stick that Ally was wicked good at using! Following that we took our apples and launched them out of a cannon. It was sick.

In November of 2020, Ally and I got our first place together! We found a place that was a bit of a midpoint for us, I worked in the loop and wanted somewhere I could walk to the metra. Ally worked at Advocate Christ in Oak Lawn. So this was the best bet midpoint for us! It ended up not mattering as I became a remote-worker, and comandeered our kitchen as my new home office, but nonetheless we loved the space and really loved the town.
We opened up our first event with our friends by hosting Friendsgiving. A bit of a challenge -- we had no couch for the first few months living here due to an unexpected materials shortage! Luckily we got to rent out the game room, so after some nice pictures with our friends in the apartment, we went off to a real celebration space. 
Over the year we had here we went on to create a really cozy space. See our wonderfully warm bedroom, special designed by my personal interior designer Alyssa Nicole. We had a breath-taking plant shelf, and plenty of kitchen counterspace to make sushi! Eventually we got our couch, and with some help from Tim on furniture-re-coloring, we completed our living room and made this apartment an abode.

This is also Eugene Lebron Jams' first home. Please see cute pictures of Michael Jordan Spikes (Spikechael Jordan) on the last few slides. Squilliam Pantsyson appreciates your support.

In 2021, we took on winter sports! We had a ski trip to Colorado planned with all of our friends, so Alyssa and I took a mini-vacation to Little Switzerland in Wisconsin to get some learning time in. We learned it's pretty similar to ice skating (use those edges!) and picked it up pretty quickly.

In February of 2021, Alyssa and I and a few of our friends got a nice big house in Granby Ranch, CO and did some skiing! This was either of our first real ski trip, so we had a ton to pack. The mountains were a ton of fun, and the views were beautiful. The runs were a lot more steep and much longer than the ones we saw in Wisconsin. It was a little scary at first, but we both adjusted quickly and flew down the mountains unscathed! 

[Highlight video](https://youtu.be/26TjUXIKvNc?si=SDxcCyqNAiBk7M9P)

Kizuna Sushi Bistro is a really cool sushi place out in the Chicago Suburbs! Something to note about this place is they have very unique rolls. Everywhere we go tends to have your usual philidephia, spicy tuna, etc... alongside some specialty rolls. But the specialty rolls here were on another level! They used special ingredients like black rice and wonton wraps to bring creative rolls to the table. If you're ever in Glenn Elynn, I'd recommend stopping by here for lunch or dinner. If you're looking for something quicker, you've gotta check out this cute mom-and-pop shop Olive & Vinnie's. They've got an amazing peanut butter snack that absolutely slaps

---
**S Tier** - Sushi Dokku (West Loop) (Same as booze box), 🍣Ohshima (Los Angeles, CA)

**A Tier** - Kura (Schaumburg), Sushi-san, Sushi Taku (Wicker Park), Maple and ash (Gold Coast)

**B Tier** - **Kizuna sushi bistro (Glenn Elynn)**, Sushi Ukai (La Grange), Wild Tuna (Naperville), Sushi Time (Elmhurst), Sakanaya (Champaign), Kamehachi (Gold Coast)

**C Tier** - Umami sushi (O’Hare), Sushi + (Lakeview), Shakou (Park Ridge), Mizu Sushi House (Orland Park)

**F** - Wu’s House (Orland Park x 2) (BAD, DO NOT COME BACK)

---

Elmhurst has a bunch of gems in town to eat at, and one of the many is Victory Meat and Seafood. Around this time Ally and I had grown a real hankering for oysters. We've been raw fish people for forever, but only recently started indulging in oysters. We were ecstatic to find out there was an oyster-serving place right down the street from us!

For my 25th birthday, Ally and I decided it'd be fun to make a quick trip out to Florida and visit Discovery Cove! I had never heard of the place before, so Ally was my sherpa. The place is really cool, we get free drinks and food in the park, and there's a large snorkeling area where you get to dive with all kinds of fish!

Our next stop in Florida was Downtown Disney! Despite all the times I had been to Disneyworld, I never even knew downtown disney existed! It was a really cool place to walk though. It's a really awesome nightlife option, way more lively than I was expecting! I thought it would be a little shopping with a disney theme, but it ended up being like a small city with live music, drinks, and lots of fun snacks. We got to stop by Gideon's Bakehouse, which had these HUGE decadent cookies. They were pretty good, but in all honesty, it was too sweet to finish. I think it's worth trying, but be ready to split a cookie between 2-4 people!

The main event of our Florida trip, Epcot! We visited Epcot and went for drinks around the world. Mid-covid, so we have masks on the whole time, but we didn't let that spoil our fun! 

In picture order, we got to see...
* Spaceship Earth geosphere
* The Seas with Nemo
* Lunch at the aquarium
* Epcot's hydroponic on-site farm
* Chichen-Itza Epcot (which we would see the real one just a few months later!)
* God of the Vikings
* China Pavilion
* Epcot France
* Epcot Japan
* a phone booth

At each country at epcot we got a different drink, called "Drinks around the world". By the last location we were fairly intoxicated and our feet were sore. Epcot was an absolute blast and it made our hotel room that much comfier when we were all done!

The Chocolate Museum & Cafe was actually a quick stop we had just before going off to Downtown Disney and Epcot. Again we had found a quick GroupOn and thought, why not? We love chocolate! Right when we got there I thought for a second we were at the wrong place -- it's pretty small, and the front looks like any ol' cafe. But once you walk in the place is pretty deep! We arrived about half an hour early for our tour, so we got a mini chocolate fondue pot and had a little dessert-for-brunch. After our meal, our tour started, and we got to learn about chocolate! They had a full lifecycle of the cocoa bean to chocolate, chocolate processing factory view through some glass, and at the end we got to taste some chocolate and get our very own bar! Following the tour, they let us into a room with all kinds of chocolate sculptures, like the Eiffell Tower and Chichen Itza. It was a fun little experience, and we'll always take the route with more chocolate!

The Elmhurst Art Museum is a charming little museum set in Elmhurst. They showcase all kinds of art which rotates regularly, we've gone about 3 times now I believe, and each time the exhibits were very different! The picture you see now was a mini-golf exhibit, where artists took out-of-the-box takes on mini golf. They were pretty goofy, some playing like Plinko, while others were like a ball going through a tiny golf-ball-mansion. It was a really interesting exhibit! Also here, which is not shown in pictures, is the McCormick house! It's a modular house ideated by architect by Miles van der Rohe which was to assist in solving housing issues. The idea was to have a small, affordable, mass-produced modular home. Really interesting solution to a common problem, and the Elmhurst Art Museum has a full-size model for us to explore.

Welcome to the Salem Common! This is a park in Salem, MA in which a few scenes Hocus Pocus was filmed. The park itself is nice, it's like any other park with a big open field, some sports-courts, and a big walkable path surrounding the perimeter. Scroll through the pictures here and see Alyssa recreate some movie magic!

The Schooner Fame is a sailboat out near Salem. It is a full-scale replica of the first American privateer schooner to go to battle in the War of 1812. This was the first thing we did after landing in Massachussetts -- we're pretty landlocked in Illinois, so when we have the opportunity to get on the ocean, we take it! The sail included a short history lesson, as well as an on-board cannon demonstration to see how the schooner was used in battle. We had never gone sailing before so the whole experience was a lot of fun!

We visited Salem in September of 2021 -- close enough to Halloween to feel the spook, but not so close that the town would be overrun! Salem was a fascinating town. Alyssa had wanted to go as she LOVES Hocus Pocus, as well as Salem being a top-tier Autumn Ally Spooky town. The town really leans into the Salem Witch Trials history. The police and firemen on their badges actually have a witch riding a broom as the logo. You can find witch statues everywhere you look, and many protected places of history based on the witch trials. You'll find graveyards or homes of judges who prosecuted witches, or the homes of the women who were accused of being witches. 
We stayed at The Hotel Salem, which was nicely right in the center of everything interesting in Salem. I'd definitely recommend the hotel for the location. We were able to walk to the Schooner Fame, various witch museums, several protected Salem Witch Trials-related buildings, and get to the train all from this spot! Salem can honestly be covered in a weekend, it's a town that is it's own little witchy bubble. A unique, interesting experience and I'd recommend to anyone who's interested in the witch trials!

_"Be spooky. Enjoyed"_ - Alyssa Nicole

We stayed in Salem for a weekend, and finished most of the items we wanted to do in Salem pretty quickly. We found that Boston was a quick train ride from Salem, so on our last morning there before flying out, we took a train out to Boston for a day trip. The first picture is at the New England Aquarium. It's no Shedd, but it was still a pretty cool place! It was multi-level, I think something like 4 floors, with plenty of interesting exhibits. Our favorite part was the penguins! There's a center spot of the aquarium in which they have a LARGE space for pengiuns to dive, swim, or chill on some false icebergs. Following that we went to explore Boston, we were hoping to do The Freedom Trail, but unfortunately we caught pretty bad weather and couldn't follow through. Instead we opted to check out the Boston Common and the Harvard Campus. I'll be straight up, Harvard was a pretty lame campus. We both went there expecting a pretty prestigious place but the quad and buildings were fairly underwhelming. Maybe they're different on the inside? Anyways, Boston itself was a really great city to see. A ton of history surrounding it, and very walkable and tourist friendly!

Kamehachi is a pretty fanci sushi bar out in Old Town. We found this place as we were going to the Immersive Van Gogh exhibit just west of here. The restaurant was great, they seated us outside on a really nice day. The sushi was solid, but the real highlight was the "Oyster shot"! It was raw oyster with yolk, sounded pretty weird but it was delicious!

Dreams Jade was an __okay__ all-inclusive. This was, I believe the 4th all-inclusive we'd gone to. The beach was beautiful, and we had a wonderful time walking up and down the beach and chit-chatting. If you got to the end of the beach, you'd actually find a swim-with-the-dolphins section right off the water. The worst part was the aggressive sales tactics; it was the least all-inclusive vacation we had gone to as everywhere you went, they tried to upsell you on extra features! I definitely will never go to anther Dreams all inclusive, but that we still made the best of it, and had a wonderfully relaxing time!

Chichén-Itzá is one of two excursions we went on during this trip to Mexico. It's a Mayan city, with the center being Kukulcan temple, which was used for astrological endeavors and religious ceremonies. The city also had a Great Ball Court and architecture depicting decapitated skulls!

Quintana Roo is the second excursion we went on this vacation, and it was really cool! We went out to visit Xel-Ha, as well as see some of the deepest cenotes in Mexico. Xel-Ha was really beautiful, being on top of a bit of a hill and overlooking the water. The cenote was both fascinating and horrifying -- it was deep and dark, but diving in it was a trip! The water was so blue and the cave was surprisingly vivid inside. After the cenote we got to go snorkeling in a laguna with more fish! It felt like the big-time version of when we went to Discovery Cove. Finally, after our long day, we got dinner in Quintana Roo at the Punta Venado Beach club where Alyssa got some of the most delicious ceviche that she still talks about monthly!

In April of 2022, we went out to Arizona! Our first stop here was Page Springs Cellars for a winery tour and wine tasting. We got to see their fields, which I didn't expect to see a full vineyard in the middle of Arizona! After that they showed us their wine aging process, and their cellar filled with wine barrels. The location overlooks long rolling fields of green leading off into the sunset. It's a great place to enjoy a glass of wine and the beautiful scenery of the Arizona desert.

The Grand Canyon really lived up to its' name! When we went to visit we knew it would be stunning, but it really is in its' own category of natural wonders. We opted to start off our visit with a Pink Jeep tour! It really stunned us the first step out of the pink jeep to see just how deep and far the canyon went. We went off to the visitor center and got some nice souveneirs and continued on to hit up a hike! The altitude really slaps you, the downhill was more than fine but on our way up we had to take more than a few breaks just to catch our breath! We weren't tired as much as we were just low on oxygen. Or maybe the canyon was just _truly breathtaking._

column1: Verde River Greenway State Natural Area
column4: The next day we went off to the Verde River, where we went on a horseback ride to a train, which is the only way across the Verde Canyon Railroad. The train ride was interesting, we were hoping to see some wildlife given there is no infrastructure out there, but we really just saw a bunch of rocks. You could tell this was common, as they had dedicated train staff to identify rocks which looked like objects, as if they were reading clouds in the sky. "That one up there, to the left, just above that tree. That's a turtle." "You see that? Up to the right, just near that cave, and then down a bit. Yeah, that's fonzie. AAAYYYYYY". Admittedly I ended up taking a short train nap, but the overall experience was unique and a nice notch under our belts! We ended our day on a short hike overlooking Cathedral Rock, and hungout there through sunset.

Sedona, AZ, the city in which I proposed to Alyssa! On the morning of April 15th, 2022, I asked Alyssa to put on some nice clothes for a hot air balloon ride through Sedona. We got to the "flight location" just before sunrise, where we met a few groups of people prepping hot air balloons. The wind that morning didn't seem like it was going to work out for us; they started blowing up balloons and letting them free to see if the wind was carrying the right way. There's no steering hot air balloons, you just go up or down and hope for the best! I was getting a bit nervous at this point; my whole proposal plan was banking on this. Luckily, about half an hour later, they called us ready to fly and they started blowing up the balloons. We got up in the air and the view was beautiful! We clutched on tight to the basket and overlooked Sedona and its surrounding scenic rim. After about an hour or so, we started our bumpy landing. Once on the ground, I took Alyssa to the side to enjoy the view while they started packing up the hot air balloon into vans. We chatted for a short minute before I got down on one knee and proposed. Honestly, neither of us remembers what I even said in that moment. We both blacked out of nervousness! But thankfully she said yes, and here we are now!

Afterwards we took off our coats and took a bunch of pictures to remember the moment. About a year before this, Ally let me know she thought it'd be hilarious to take pictures with a ring pop to accompany our proposal pics. Big thanks to Alyssa and Promit for taking all the pics for us. Enjoy our post-proposal pictures feat. Ring Pop!

After the proposal outing, we still had plenty of daylight! So we went back out to Devil's Bridge. This was actually a spot I had considered proposing at, but after some research, I learned this is a VERY popular spot, and there's usually a line to get up to the trailhead, as well as a big crowd who would watch the proposal. Ally had talked about wanting a fairly private proposal in the past, so I knew this wasn't it. Luckily the hot air balloon trip worked out, and it didn't come down to this! The reviews were accurate and we had a decent wait in line for pictures before the ones you see here. Nonetheless, the spot was really cool! "Devil's Bridge" is a perfect name. It's a rock formation about four stories high, with the bridge being a thin connection between two towers. It was pretty sweaty to get up there to take a picture, but worth the photo op!

Rockwell on the River was the stunning wedding venue of my best man, Akash! He and his wife Anu hosted Alyssa and me at an incredible multi-day Indian wedding. I was lucky enough to support him as his best man as well. It was a ton of fun learning the traditions and dances throughout the time, and MAN were the decorations beautiful!

In June of 2022, Alyssa and I, as well as her sister Jillian, took my father-in-law Tim to Busse Lake for a nice day of kayaking! We went across the lake and enjoyed the time on the water. We saw some tadpoles, chased some birds, and (Tim and I) did a lot of paddling!

One day in June we were passing by this cocktail bar, Machine: Engineered! Ally had mentioned seeing this on Tiktok before, so we knew we had to stop in and check it out. We both got some cocktails and had a nice little date! The cocktails were interesting, shown here Alyssa's was shaped like a bird, and my own was a drink with a crystallized sugar ball accompanied by a tiny mallet! I was to crush the ball to make my drink sweeter. Really interesting place, and made for a fun date!

In September-October of 2022, we had our engagement photos scheduled. We were originally planning to have some photos in the upper peninsula of Michigan but ended up taking them in Benton Harbor instead. Nonetheless, we decided to plan a trip up there anyways! Our chosen spot was Mackinac Island -- a favorite vacation spot of my dad's. The island was amazing, it's an island with no cars allowed! Everyone traveled by horseback for longer trips, or snowmobile in the winter. The island is only about 5 square miles, and there's a nice 8-mile biking trail around the perimeter. We had some nice hikes, explored the town, and got on a tandem bike to ride the trail!

St. Joseph is a town we've been to more than a few times now. In 2022 the Jordan's decided to buy a boat, and Tim has been nice enough to take us on it a couple times a year! It's always a good time being on the water, and with some good music, good people, and good drinks, it's a great time!

Benton Harbor is the home to a nice park and scenic beach! We came here for our engagement photos a couple months after the proposal, and MAN did they come out beautiful. Big thank you to Michael Koch, who is here today as our photographer!

In 2022 our pumpkin patch/orchard of choice was Goebbert's Farm. Delicious apple cider treats and as always, a cute petting zoo! This farm also happened to host a ton of corn kernels that Ally couldn't resist grabbing a bucket of!

Despite living nearby and visiting every other major park, we had never been to the Morton Arboretum! We fixed this problem in November of 2022, when we got to see the Morton Arboretum Illumination. We went to several "zoo lights" or "winter park lights" shows in 2022, and Morton's was wonderfully unique! They did a lot of unique lighting around the park, finished by this projection show on a large set of trees near the end. I don't really know how else to describe it, you'll have to go see it yourself this year!

Welcome to the Jordan's! Tim and Bernice tend to host us a couple times a month, for bonfires, smoked meat BBQs, wine, dessert, or just a nice day to hangout. It's always a chill time at the Jordan's, they've got wine, beer, snacks, and dogs. I've been so lucky to have such a nice family welcome me into their home time and time again, and Alyssa and I look forward to getting a house one day and returning the favor!

In December of 2022 we went off to Joe's on Weed St. to see our favorite cover band, Rod Tuffcurls and the Bench Press! We had first seen them at UIUC, and later on in life we had our mutual friends who were still fairly passionate about seeing them (brett)! As good of friends we are, we accompany our friends to shows, and naturally gained a passion for the shows ourselves. It's always a blast, Rod plays BANGERS and we've never been to a show we didn't absolutely love. This was probably the ninth or tenth show we had gone to, and somehow this is the first time we got a picture! Guess we just spend too much time *PARTYING!*

For New Year's 2022, our friends Kira and Max hosted us! Before going to their place to watch some Navy Pier fireworks and playing some JackBox, we went to Athena Greek restaurant. This place was delicious! I ate so much lamb I got the meat sweats. We had some wine and great conversation, it was one of our more heartwarming wholesome New Year's.

For our *final* dating anniversary, we went to Booze Box for Omakase. This, by far, is our favorite sushi we've ever had. Our Omakase Chef Zach did an incredible job. A few months before this dinner, we listed our sushi preferences and what we liked in general, and Zack crafted a special menu just for us. He's a 15+ year experienced sushi chef, and an established Omakase chef at Boozebox. Each bite was so unique and so delicious, we were both wildly impressed by his skills. He was able to put together such interesting flavors using marinade, the cut of the fish, greens, and more! I'd have to say Zack's take on Suzuki or Hamachi was my favorite. Alyssa loved his Shima Aji. He closed off our meal with A5 Wagyu, and the quality was better than some of the high-end Chicago steakhouses I visited. We loved it so much that we took the menu, framed it, and have it hung up in our kitchen today.

_"sushi was good, 10/10 would come back"_ - Alyssa Nicole

Ally and I are fans of mini golf, and having live pretty near Oakbrook, we've passed Puttshack more than a few times. We finally took the time to check it out in February of 2023! It was a lot of fun, it was like the professional version of the artsy mini golf we did at Elmhurst Art Museum. The balls all have trackers in them, and each hole has a special scoring system. The main fun of it though, is how unique each hole is, and having drinks while we walked through it!

column1: Wagyu House by The X Pot Chicago
column4: For Valentine's day in 2023, Ally and I decided to try out Wagyu at the X Pot Chicago. It was definitely the fanciest hot pot we've ever been to. We like hot pot, our hot pot of choice is Happy Lamb Hot Pot, who we think has the best broth of all the hot pot's we've gone to. This place, X Pot, definitely had the best meat though! We ate so much wagyu we felt sick afterwards, which *I* thought was totally worth it. Alyssa would beg to differ. I don't blame her, I felt terrible. Anyways, the wagyu on the gold bull was really cool, and it was a nice place to spend a few hours and be able to take Alyssa out to a special dinner.

BomboBar is a pretty cool bar out in Gold Coast. Ally and I went here with our friends Alyssa and Promit while they were in town! We had a few fancy cocktails and sat and chatted for hours. Ally and Alyssa talked about the wedding, and Promit and I contemplated that _if we're in a simulation, is it ethical to have a set of people to ensure our health of the main body?_ Towards the end of the night Ally and I found a sweet full body mirror near the bathrooms and took this cute pic. With the chaos of wedding planning, we hadn't had a nice date night at the bars in awhile, so this was a welcome night.

Bob Chinn is the king of garlic. Ally took me here for my birthday dinner and MAN was it absolutely delicious. She had gone here with her family a few times, and they always mentioned how garlicky everything was. They knew it was the perfect place for me! So we get here and get the biscuits, and it comes in a basket full of minced garlic, and wow was it incredible. We had some seafood as our entrees and I requested extra garlic, and they definitely complied! Our server was very sweet, and it was actually her birthday coming up soon too! She made sure to wash our cups and let us keep them as a birthday souvenir. I cannot wait to come back here, this is one of my favorite restaurants, thank you Alyssa!!!

Kind of a weird one here, but this is Napleton's Palatine Mazda! Not like the others, this is actually on the list as this is where we bought our first car together. Both of our cars were getting fairly old and my truck in particular wasn't fitting for our style of living (I worked from home, and didn't really haul materials). So I traded in my truck, and we got a 2015 Honda CR-V! Admittedly it's had its' share of problems, but no big purchase is perfect, and we love this car nonetheless! It's made our commutes that much easier, and wow it is noticeable how much better a newer car drives! We were so proud fo have done so much research and land on a vehicle we both really liked, we went out and got lychee cocktails at one of our favorite Chinese food places shortly after.

In July of 2023, we attended the Dziedzina wedding! This took place at Loft Lucia, and was another magnificent wedding. The ceremony was half-outdoors, and was so wholesome! It was really cool seeing the traditions they included, and the dance floor was a JAM! I don't have much to say outside of that, the wedding was so perfect from start to finish, alyssa and I got plenty of slow-and-fast dancing in and ate delicious food and talked with good friends. What else could you ask for at a wedding?

In August of 2023, Ally and I attended the Shull wedding! I was honored as a Groomsman for this one. Joel and Becca had gotten the whole bridal party an Airbnb for the weekend, and it was an incredible time! We hungout in hot tubs, played bags, scream-rapped some songs, and just sat around and chatted for days. Each night melted into the next day as we all had such a fun time hanging out every night. This all came into a beautiful summit on the day of the wedding. Becca and Joel had their wedding at Cooper's Cove, which was a beautiful outdoor ceremony followed by a reception inside. We danced for hours, cleaned up, and carried on the party for a few more hours back at the Airbnb! At the end of the weekend, we all said goodbyes despite how little we wanted to leave. So thankful for this experience and to have the Shulls in our lives.

We stayed at The Hyatt Lodge in Oakbrook for the Kreiter wedding! Max and Kira threw a pulchritudinous wedding. Alyssa and I rocked it with our matching blues! Their ceremony was outside on a beautiful day, followed by a cocktail hour nearby, also partially outdoors! This is when these fantastic outdoor photos were taken (PC: Elyse + Lester). We had a wonderful time eating hors d'oeuvres and sipping drinks. We went inside for the reception and MAN do they know how to party. Absolute bangers throughout the night, I wouldn't expect anything less from these two. They are two of the best hosts to ever do it, and we were so happy to celebrate their love together!
